RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Harper Novak
Member ID: W970661607
Reference Number: POC-321500D934-38813
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-07-31
Requested Service: Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
Treating Surgeon: [Dr.] Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130), as communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-07-31. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity."

I want to note at the outset that the denial notice does not identify, quote, or cite the specific medical policy or clinical criteria document used to evaluate this request, nor does it specify which items of documentation were considered missing or insufficient. I have been unable to independently locate a single, publicly available Georgia Medicaid policy document specific to CPT 27130 that was cited as the basis for this determination. I am therefore not able to respond to specific plan policy language, because none was quoted to me or made available. I respectfully request, pursuant to my right to the criteria used in this determination, that the plan identify the exact medical policy (title, policy number, and version/effective date) and the specific documentation gaps relied upon for this denial, in writing.

In the meantime, and to avoid delay in my care, I am submitting the following clinical documentation from my prior authorization packet, which I believe addresses medical necessity for total hip replacement:

1. Symptom duration and severity: I have experienced 9 months of progressive hip pain that is unrelieved by rest.

2. Conservative treatment — physical therapy: I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-04-09 through 2026-06-04), totaling 20 visits, focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait training. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note, which is [attached/available and being submitted with this appeal].

3. Conservative treatment — medication and injection: I was treated with NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-12, which provided only 2 weeks of partial relief.

4. Imaging findings: A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph obtained 2026-06-13 shows joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes, consistent with advanced degenerative joint disease.

5. Functional limitation: I currently ambulate with a cane, am limited to walking one block, and cannot put on my shoes unassisted.

6. Physical examination: Exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.

7. Absence of contraindications: There is no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder. My BMI is 29. I am a non-smoker.

Taken together, this record documents nine months of symptomatic hip osteoarthritis, a completed and well-documented trial of conservative management (physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection) that has failed to provide durable relief, radiographic confirmation of advanced joint space narrowing with sclerosis and osteophyte formation, and significant functional impairment affecting activities of daily living. My treating orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has recommended total hip replacement (CPT 27130) based on this clinical picture.

If any specific document (e.g., the physical therapy discharge note, imaging report, or injection record) was missing from the original submission, I am prepared to promptly supply it. I ask that the plan specify exactly what was incomplete so that this can be corrected without further delay, given the impact of this condition on my mobility and daily functioning.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in the denial notice (received within 180 days of the notice date, i.e., by 2027-01-27). However, I understand that Georgia Medicaid managed-care appeal deadlines may in some cases be shorter (e.g., 60 calendar days from the date of the notice), so I am filing this appeal promptly and request written confirmation that it has been received and is being treated as timely.

Please provide:
- Written confirmation of receipt of this appeal;
- The specific medical policy or clinical criteria (title, policy number, and effective date) applied to this request;
- An itemized list of any documentation still considered missing or insufficient; and
- The outcome of this appeal in writing, including appeal rights to a State Fair Hearing if the denial is upheld.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal. Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] if any additional information is needed.

Sincerely,

Harper Novak
Member ID: W970661607

Enclosures:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-09 to 2026-06-04)
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph and report (2026-06-13)
- Medication and injection records
- Surgeon's office notes and exam findings (Dr. Lindqvist)
- [Any additional records requested by the plan]
